title: Five songs students should know
summary: Blues, rhythm changes and standards like My Shining Hour; young players know 1960s Herbie and Wayne Shorter tunes instead.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: What do you tell your students, five songs that you’d better know or don’t go to any jam sessions.
Five songs. Well one is the blues two is rhythm changes,

It’s a hard list. [inaudible] like “My Shining Hour,” “It Could Happen to You,” maybe “One Finger Snap,” you know, tunes like that. Because most of the young kids don’t know the repertoire of the standards or they’re really into the records more of like Herbie and Wayne Shorter, you know sixties, tunes like — what’s that tune — “Black Nile” and tunes like that.
It seems like in New York anyway, because kids are into that now.
